Subject: Initial: Retention & sanitize options for PHI in Redwood Private

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks for the overview call earlier. We're finalizing our security and legal checklist ahead of a pilot and need a short, clear summary of the retention and redaction options Redwood can commit to for PHI in a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Specifically can you confirm the following and point us to any attestation/artifact we can include in our procurement packet: 

- Retention windows supported (examples: 30 / 90 / 365 / custom) and whether Redwood can enforce tenant-level retention cutoffs that automatically purge underlying storage.
- Soft-delete vs hard-delete semantics: Is there an immutable window where data is recoverable? How long and can this be disabled?
- Redaction options before persistence: field-level masking, tokenization, deterministic pseudonymization, one-way hashing, or full record redaction. Which are available in-line (pre-store) versus post-hoc (on-demand scrub)?
- Legal hold / eDiscovery: ability to place a temporary preservation hold that overrides retention. Audit trail for holds.
- Proof of deletion / deletion certification: is there a verifiable artifact we can store (audit log entry, signed attestation)?
- Evidence for compliance: SOC2 artifacts, sample data-flow diagram for Private deployment, KMS usage + HSM attestations.

Attachments: sample_evidence_checklist.pdf (our internal checklist) and a simple data_flow_diagram.png that shows how our app routes requests to Redwood Private.

We'd appreciate a short decision-tree style doc (one page) describing recommended configurations depending on whether the goal is: (A) regulatory retention (retain some de-identified records for X days); (B) minimal retention (delete asap); (C) audit-heavy (retain logs but remove PHI). Can you also flag any limitations for on-prem installs vs Redwood hosted?

Thanks — looking to close procurement approvals by mid-July.

Best,
Emily

Emily — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick summary below; I've attached a concise options PDF and a draft decision tree. Happy to walk through this with Legal/Sec next week.

High level answers (short-form):
- Retention windows: Redwood Private supports tenant-level retention policies with configurable TTLs. Common presets: 30/90/365 days or a custom ISO8601 duration. Enforcement: yes — the control plane issues lifecycle jobs to purge objects after TTL expiry for supported storage backends. (See attached for storage backends matrix.)
- Soft-delete vs hard-delete: We support soft-delete for a configurable grace period (default 30d). Hard delete is available once the grace period expires or immediately via an admin purge API; on some on-prem storage configs irreversible deletion may require manual wipe if using third-party archival.
- Redaction options:
  * In-line pre-store: field-level masking (client-side or transform pipeline) and deterministic pseudonymization (tokenization) are supported via our ingestion hooks before events reach storage.
  * Post-hoc: one-way hashing and bulk scrubbing jobs are available, but these are post-process and may leave derived caches intact until invalidated.
- Legal hold: Yes — can place a preservation hold that prevents lifecycle purges. Holds are auditable and scoped to tenant or dataset.
- Proof of deletion: Audit logs include TTL and deletion job entries; for Dedicated/Private we can generate a deletion report and optional signed attestation (requires enterprise contract).
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 report excerpts are available under NDA; for Private we'll provide a deployment-specific data-flow diagram and KMS usage notes (we support cloud KMS and customer-supplied HSM integration).

Limits / tradeoffs to flag:
- On-hosted Redwood (managed) gives the tightest automation for purge and attestation; Private requires an operations step for some archival connectors.
- Inline redaction best practice is client-side or ingestion-hook transform (we provide examples). Post-hoc scrubbing can be slower and might require offline validation.

Next steps:
1) I attached a short options PDF (redwood-retention-sanitization-options-v1.pdf) and a draft decision-tree (decision-tree-draft.drawio.png).
2) Suggest a 30-minute legal + security sync next Tue or Wed — link to a short availability poll: https://app.redwood.ai/share/ddc123

If useful, we can scope a simple attestation deliverable in the SOW for the pilot.

Regards,

Adding a few technical clarifications for Emily — short bullets so Legal can see tradeoffs: 

- Caching: application-level prefix/KV caching lives outside the primary retention lifecycle by default; you must explicitly flush caches when you purge source records. We provide an API to invalidate model KV entries and prefix caches but clients must call it or enable automatic invalidation policies.
- Sequence length / model caches: local KV caches used for inference (e.g., for long conversations) are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage unless configured to do so; treat them as transient but mention them in your data flow.
- Backups & snapshots: Depending on storage, backups may still retain copies — purge jobs attempt to scrub snapshots but some snapshot systems require separate retention config. We'll document recommended snapshot policies for on-prem object stores.
- KMS/HSM: For Private you can use a customer-managed KMS; keys can be rotated per policy and key-wrapping is supported. If you require HSM attestation, we'll coordinate with SecOps to exchange certs.

I'll join the legal sync to field technical follow-ups.

-Marissa

Emily — great questions, quick answers and proposed call agenda:

Implementation effort: minimal config + ingestion-hook script for pseudonymization; we can scope a 1-2 week engineering task to harden the pipeline for production and add tests.
